To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the administration of DIP followed by low-dosage maintenance immunotherapy was effective and safe for patients with recurrent or metastatic squamous cell cancer of the head and/or neck, and that lymphocyte and natural killer cell counts increased, while VEGF decreased, during maintenance immunotherapy.
a combination chemotherapy regimen followed by maintenance immunotherapy is an effective treatment for recurrent/metastatic head and neck cancer.
maintenance immunotherapy is a promising strategy in the treatment of patients with RMHN.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and testing of new treatments for cancer.
the use of immunotherapy to improve the treatment of cancer patients.
the use of maintenance immunotherapy in recurrent/metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of docetaxel/ifosfamide/cisplatin and maintenance immunotherapy is an effective treatment for RMHN, and that the combination of low-dose interleucin-2 and low-dose 13-cis retinoic acid may be useful as maintenance immunotherapy in patients with RMHN.
maintenance immunotherapy in patients with RMHN who showed clinical benefit after DIP chemotherapy is safe, feasible, and effective.
maintenance immunotherapy with low dose IL-2 and 9-cis retinoic acid in combination with DIP is a promising treatment for patients with recurrent/metastic squamous cell carcinoma head and neck.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new regimen for RMHN, which is based on a novel concept that combines chemotherapy and maintenance immunotherapy, and we have demonstrated that it is feasible and safe and that it has a promising activity and a good toxicity profile.

the maintenance immunotherapy regimen of interleukin-12 and retinoic acid, which was administered in the present study, was generally well-tolerated and had promising activity against RMHNS, with the potential to improve the prognosis of patients with RMHNS who showed a clinical response to DIP chemotherapy.

we have shown a promising efficacy of a maintenance immunomodulatory therapy in patients with recurrent or metastatic squamous cell carcinomas of the head and Neck who have shown a clinical benefit from a chemotherapy regimen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
maintenance immunotherapy is safe and effective in RMHN.
a maintenance immunotherapy with interleukin- 2 and 13- cis-retinoic acid after DIP can be used to improve survival in patients with recurrent and metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
maintenance therapy can be administered in a safe and effective fashion to patients who are responding to chemotherapy.
